description:
The Royal Palace of Portici sits on the Bay of Naples, begun in 1738 for Charles of Bourbon, King of Naples, after the discoveries at ancient Herculaneum drew the royal court to the area. The Duke of Elbeuf's digging near his own property nearby had already marked the beginning of the exploration of Herculaneum, and Charles chose to build his new residence close to the excavations rather than elsewhere on the bay.

Construction passed through several architects: Giovanni Antonio Medrano led the early works, Antonio Canevari took over direction in 1741, and Luigi Vanvitelli and Ferdinando Fuga both intervened at later stages. Sources give either 1742 or 1743 as the completion date. The palace became the seat of the Herculanense Museum, opened in 1758 to house finds from Herculaneum and the other Vesuvian sites, and the combination of royal residence and antiquities collection made Portici a destination for Grand Tour travellers visiting Naples.

Today the Royal Palace of Portici is part of the University of Naples Federico II. The GetYourGuide ticket covers entry to the palace, the Royal Apartments, the Herculanense Museum and the botanical gardens on the grounds, alongside a round-trip train ticket from Naples. Some rooms may open only on weekends, so check the official site for which areas are open on the day of your visit.
history: Charles of Bourbon, King of Naples, began the palace at Portici in 1738 after the discoveries at ancient Herculaneum drew the court to the area; Giovanni Antonio Medrano led the early works and Antonio Canevari took over in 1741, with Luigi Vanvitelli and Ferdinando Fuga intervening later. The king bought neighbouring villas and extended the site towards the sea. The palace housed the Herculanense Museum, opened in 1758 for finds from the Vesuvian sites and a destination on the Grand Tour. It is now part of the University of Naples Federico II.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** The GetYourGuide meeting point is the tourist services desk (inStazione servizi turistici) at Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi, 80142 Naples; the ticket includes the round-trip train from Naples to Portici.

**Tickets:** The GetYourGuide ticket (€19 per person) bundles the round-trip train ticket, entry to the palace, the Royal Apartments, the Herculanense Museum and the botanical gardens, with a downloadable guide app and free cancellation up to 24 hours before; guided tours, food, drinks, tips and earphones are not included. Opening hours and entry fees vary by source, so check the official site before you go.

**Practical tips:** Collect your tickets at the inStazione tourist office at Piazza Garibaldi. The visit is at your own pace on the selected date. Some areas may open only on weekends, so check which parts are open on your day.

**Combine with:** Naples' own castles and palaces — [Castel Nuovo](/castles/italy/castel-nuovo), [Naples Royal Palace](/castles/italy/naples-royal-palace) and the [Royal Palace of Caserta](/castles/italy/royal-palace-of-caserta).

faqs.question: Why is the Royal Palace of Portici linked to Herculaneum?
faqs.answer: The Duke of Elbeuf's digging near his property began the exploration of Herculaneum, and Charles of Bourbon's court was drawn to Portici; the palace became the seat of the Herculanense Museum, opened in 1758 to hold the finds.

faqs.question: Does the ticket include the train from Naples?
faqs.answer: Yes. The GetYourGuide ticket includes a round-trip train ticket from Naples, plus entry to the palace, the Royal Apartments, the Herculanense Museum and the botanical gardens.
